overview: This file documents two related aspects of the postwar circulation and preservation of Japanese newspapers. Most of the papers concern State Department efforts to place a nearly complete Tokyo file of the Japanese-language Mainichi Shimbun, dating from June 17, 1917, with an American research library: Harvard declined, after which Yale and the Hoover Library were approached, and Hoover expressed interest. A second sequence records the American Consulate General in São Paulo's request to discontinue the official supply of Japanese newspapers to the local Japanese community because normal communications with Japan had improved sufficiently. The bundle includes correspondence, internal memoranda, routing and telephone notes, a consular despatch, and a Department of State instruction dating from December 1948 through May 1949.

subfiles.title: Letter to Yale offering the Mainichi Shimbun collection
subfiles.from: Lawrence S. Morris, Acting Chief, Division of Libraries and Institutes
subfiles.to: James T. Babb, Librarian, Yale University Library
subfiles.about: Morris asks whether Yale wishes to pursue the purchase of a nearly complete file of the Japanese-language Mainichi Shimbun available in Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: State offers Yale a near-complete Mainichi Shimbun archive, war-damaged but intact, priced at several hundred thousand yen.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on Harvard's preliminary interest in the Mainichi Shimbun
subfiles.from: C. E. Walton, Division of Libraries and Institutes
subfiles.about: Walton reports a conversation with Harvard Library staff about the newspaper collection described in Sebald's letter from Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: Harvard's Osborn finds the Mainichi archive's price reasonable, pending Fairbank's opinion.

subfiles.title: Routing note proposing Yale and Hoover as alternate purchasers
subfiles.from: Unidentified Department officials, including JHE and S. W.
subfiles.about: The note records Buchanan's absence and recommends approaching Yale and then the Hoover Library if Harvard does not proceed.
subfiles.summary: Note suggests offering the Mainichi archive to Yale, then the Hoover Library, if Harvard declines.

subfiles.title: Routing record for the newspaper-collection file
subfiles.about: A brief routing record notes the transfer and filing of the matter concerning the Japanese newspaper collection.
subfiles.summary: Routing slip logs internal file movement for the newspaper-archive acquisition correspondence.

subfiles.title: Contact note for Walton's temporary replacement
subfiles.from: Unidentified Department of State staff member
subfiles.about: The note supplies contact details for the staff member temporarily replacing Walton.
subfiles.summary: Note names a temporary contact for the newspaper-archive inquiry while the usual officer is away.

subfiles.title: Follow-up note on the delayed Harvard reply
subfiles.about: Buchanan records a telephone conversation with Walton concerning Harvard's delayed decision.
subfiles.summary: Note records Harvard hasn't yet replied on the Mainichi archive offer, with a reply expected soon.

subfiles.title: Telephone message from Miss Wallace about Walton's memorandum
subfiles.about: A telephone-message form records a call from Miss Wallace concerning Walton's memorandum.
subfiles.summary: Message slip logs a call concerning Walton's memo on the newspaper-archive acquisition.

subfiles.title: Notes recording Harvard's rejection and further referrals
subfiles.about: The notes record Harvard's decision not to buy the papers and the plan to approach Yale or Hoover.
subfiles.summary: Notes record Harvard declining the Mainichi archive, suggesting Yale or Hoover as alternatives.

subfiles.title: Letter to Hoover Library offering the Mainichi Shimbun collection
subfiles.from: Lawrence S. Morris, Acting Chief, Division of Libraries and Institutes
subfiles.to: Nina Almond, Hoover Library on War, Revolution and Peace
subfiles.about: Morris asks whether the Hoover Library wishes to pursue the purchase of the Mainichi Shimbun file in Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: State offers the Hoover Library the same Mainichi archive, war-damaged but intact, at the same price.

subfiles.title: Attached memorandum on Harvard's preliminary interest
subfiles.from: C. E. Walton, Division of Libraries and Institutes
subfiles.about: An attached copy recounts Harvard Library's initial consideration of the Mainichi Shimbun offer.
subfiles.summary: Memo repeats that Harvard's Osborn found the price reasonable but wants Fairbank's opinion before replying.

subfiles.title: Despatch requesting an end to official newspaper supplies to São Paulo
subfiles.from: Cecil H. P. Cross, American Consul General at São Paulo
subfiles.about: Cross recommends discontinuing the official supply of Japanese newspapers to the Japanese community in São Paulo.
subfiles.summary: Consul asks to end wartime newspaper shipments to São Paulo's Japanese colony, now that normal channels have resumed.

subfiles.title: Instruction to Tokyo to discontinue forwarding Japanese newspapers
subfiles.to: Office of the Acting United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.about: The Department transmits the São Paulo despatch and directs the mission in Tokyo to end newspaper forwarding for the Brazilian distribution project.
subfiles.summary: State tells Tokyo to stop forwarding Japanese newspapers to São Paulo, since the emergency wartime arrangement is no longer needed.

subfiles.title: Hoover Library reply expressing interest in the Mainichi Shimbun
subfiles.from: Mary C. Wright, Curator, Far Eastern and Indian Collections
subfiles.to: Lawrence S. Morris, Acting Chief, Division of Libraries and Institutes
subfiles.about: Wright accepts the invitation to investigate the Mainichi Shimbun collection and asks to be connected with its source in Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: Hoover Library expresses interest in the Mainichi Shimbun archive, asking for contact details to pursue it.

interest: Shows postwar US efforts to place an endangered Japanese newspaper archive, and wartime press support for a diaspora community.
